title: perf(canary): improved KV hysteresis and auto-detect rollout guards
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: our performance canary has been triggering frequent false positives in high KV-cache-variance workloads, causing unnecessary rollbacks during canary rollouts. This PR updates the canary detector to include an adaptive KV hysteresis model and improved auto-detection heuristics to reduce noise while preserving sensitivity to real regressions.

What changed (summary):
- Introduced an adaptive hysteresis window for KV cache-backed models: hysteresis scales with observed KV hit-rate variance and request sequence length distribution.
- Added smoothing and outlier-resistant statistics (trimmed-mean + bootstrap CI) for P50/P95 latency and throughput signals.
- Auto-detection improvements: classifier now chooses between latency-first, throughput-first, or kv-variance-aware detection strategy based on recent workload fingerprint.
- New rollout guard rules: dynamic traffic-shift step sizing, mandatory stability window (configurable), and immediate fallback to previous model variant if P95 latency increases > 7% or tail KV miss surge > 25%.
- Runtime changes: lightweight KV metrics exporter and local buffering to avoid polluting global metrics during canary phase.
- Tests: added unit tests for hysteresis math, integration test against perf-canary harness, and end-to-end canary simulation benchmark.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc updated (ENG-1145)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Performance benchmark and sensitivity analysis attached
- [x] Observability dashboards updated
- [x] Feature flagged behind rollout_guard.v2

Testing and validation:
- Synthetic load tests across representative model sizes (1B, 7B, 13B) and KV hit/miss ratios show median false-positive rate reduced by ~78% compared to previous detector.
- Canary simulation (10k simulated requests distributed over 30 minutes with injected KV spike events) demonstrates that true regressions with >=5% P95 degrade detection latency by <2 minutes.
- Deployed behind feature flag to dedicated staging cluster for 48h with no user-facing impact; CI perf jobs and on-demand bench runs green.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main gated by rollout_guard.v2 feature flag OFF by default.
- Enable in 1% of traffic for 24h, then 10%, 50%, 100% with automatic rollback criteria enforced by the new guard rules.

Related: previous canary work (perf-canary auto-detect series), doc PR updating runbooks and SLOs.

Notes: aims to reduce noisy rollouts and give platform operators clearer diagnostics when KV-related regressions occur.
